test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: Both the Arawaks and Caribs had permanent chiefs.
The Arawaks first arrived at Saint Maarten around 1300 AD.
The Arawaks first arrived at Saint Maarten around 1000 AD.
The Carib tribe defeated the French in 1600 AD.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage states that the Arawak Indians inhabited all the islands of the West Indies 1,200 years ago.
 
• Since the current year is approximately 2025, we calculate 1,200 years ago as 2025 - 1200 = 825 AD.
 
• However, the passage also mentions that the Carib tribe defeated the Arawaks 300 years after their arrival, which means the Arawaks arrived around 1000 AD.
 
• Thus, the correct inference is that the Arawaks first arrived at Saint Maarten around 1000 AD.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **The statement is incorrect because only the Arawaks had permanent chiefs, while the Caribs had no permanent leaders except in times of strife.
 
• **Option 2: **The Arawaks did not arrive around 1300 AD; they were already settled by that time.
 
• **Option 4: **The Carib tribe did not defeat the French in 1600 AD; the French and Dutch settled the island during that time.
